body: Found while investigating why the user saw OOM-killed messages in tmux: emily-system.service (observation-watcher + emily-agent) had actually been killed by the kernel OOM killer and down for about 22 hours, with no auto-restart (one-shot systemd unit, no restart policy). Root-caused the timing to this session's earlier local GPT-2 training attempts (not the later tower-fingerprint work) - the OOM-kill landed about 10 minutes after the first local train_local.py attempt, consistent with delayed system-wide memory pressure/swap thrashing rather than direct causation. Restarted emily-system.service (freed memory first by stopping the manually-started serve.py). That surfaced a second, real problem: with Anthropic API credits exhausted (a known, accepted, pre-existing condition per founder instruction - blocked upstream on incorporation/bank accounts/revenue, not something to route around), observation-watcher was re-attempting its entire backlog of unprocessed prime tasks and observations every single 10-second poll cycle, since failed invocations never advance their cursor by design. Each attempt produced a multi-line claude CLI failure banner - pure log noise and wasted subprocess spawns on a box that had just had a real OOM incident. Fixed with a circuit breaker in cmd/observation-watcher/main.go: the first real credit-exhaustion detection (matching claude's exact 'Credit balance is too low' message) trips a 10-minute cooldown, logged once; all three invocation call sites (pollOnce for single observations, pollBatched for batched observations, pollPrimeTasks for Emily's prime task queue) check the cooldown and skip quietly while it's active, leaving cursors untouched so the real backlog gets reprocessed for real the moment the cooldown expires or credits are topped up. Also fixed, in passing: a stale process left over from an earlier kill attempt (go run's compiled child binary survives independently of its parent wrapper process and isn't matched by the same pgrep pattern used to detect it - had to kill it by PID directly). 4 new tests (isCreditExhaustedOutput matching, cooldown short-circuit without spawning a subprocess, real detection tripping the breaker via a fake failing command, and confirmation an unrelated failure does NOT trip it). Verified live, not just in tests: after restarting observation-watcher with the fix, the log went from a multi-line failure every approximately 10 seconds to zero lines for over 2 minutes (12+ poll cycles) after the breaker tripped once. Full go test ./... green across the whole PRRJECT_FATBABY module.
title: observation-watcher: credit-exhaustion circuit breaker — verified live
